dedupe_keys.name: center of tokyo results of a solar potential simulation

description: The Technical University of Munich Chair of Geoinformatics documents a solar-potential simulation for an area in central Tokyo using the PLATEAU semantic 3D city model. The official project page links the original 2020 Tokyo CityGML release and describes importing the city geometry into 3DCityDB, correcting coordinate-axis handling and transforming the horizontal reference system to JGD2011 / UTM zone 54N. The city model retains its i-Urban Revitalization application-domain-extension attributes. For the central-Tokyo demonstration, a TUM-developed tool calculated direct, diffuse and global irradiation in kWh/m² on building surfaces, including walls, and sky-view factors. Irradiation results are aggregated by building and month and displayed in an interactive 3D web map. These are model outputs for solar-resource assessment and energy-system planning, not measured generation or proof of installed photovoltaic capacity. The source states that some OuterCeilingSurfaces were deliberately omitted. The displayed case area is central Tokyo; the broader 23-ward source-data extent and 1.7-million-building total are not assumed to be the simulation extent. The simulation date and modelled meteorological year are not stated. The public project description and linked publication metadata are accessible, but no licence for the case text or computed outputs is identified and charges for reuse are not stated. A limitation is that weather inputs, numerical settings, accuracy, validation and output values were not inspected. The related PLATEAU dataset and 3DCityDB platform already exist in the catalogue. No model code, dataset, archive, article/PDF body or interactive data query was requested.

name: Center of Tokyo - Results of a Solar Potential Simulation
notes: The national PLATEAU model remains the data resource; TUM coordinate transformation, tiling and format exports are grouped as derived representations. This separate record describes the documented solar application. A prior fetch of the project HTML received a tutorial and illustrative result prose; the maintained description ends before that tutorial, as documented in retrieval-boundary.json. The linked 2017 method is a follow-up model lead; its executable identity and model classification remain unresolved.
organisations: Technical University of Munich, Chair of Geoinformatics
Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism, Japan (PLATEAU source-data provider)
outcomes: Direct, diffuse and global building-surface irradiation and sky-view factors were calculated and presented by building and month in an interactive 3D demonstration; independent accuracy and energy-generation values were not established.
provider: Technical University of Munich, Chair of Geoinformatics
